messages:
mike: FYI — we're scheduling a staggered reboot window in az9 to mitigate a thermal controller regression reported by the provider. Planned window: Fri 2026-05-14 03:00-07:00 UTC. Will run cohorts across 6 racks with 10m gap between rack cordons. Affects hosted + Dedicated pools in az9 only. No Private VPC changes expected. :thermometer_face:

alex: what does "staggered" mean operationally? any customer-facing downtime?

mike: no full outage expected. We'll cordon -> drain -> reboot -> uncordon per rack. The workload fallback policy routes to az8/az10 for latency-tolerant requests. Dedicated customers pinned to az9 will see reduced capacity during their cohort but no connection termination — just slower queueing.

sara: we should notify CS for the two large Dedicated commits in az9 (Acme + Frameo). I'll draft messages if you confirm the exact cohorts they map to.

mike: confirmed — Acme hosts mostly racks 2-3 (cohort 2), Frameo mostly rack 5 (cohort 4). Sara please include suggested mitigations: temporary burst to reserved pool in eu-west while we warm back capacity.

jordan: ops checklist — can we run a canary on a subset of kernels first? propose: pick 1 rack from cohort 1; validate nvlink, dmesg, and perf histograms for 30m before continuing.

lia: I'll handle canary. I'll also pre-warm prefix cache and KV caches for endpoints serving embeddings. Prewarm script (run from admin jump):

```
# prewarm embeddings cache (quick curl loop)
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.internal/embeddings?model=embed-v1&input=warmup-$i" >/dev/null; done
```

mike: nice. add cache warmup to runbook step 3. Also note: net team flagged intermittent NIC drop on one rack (rack-17) — we'll exclude rack-17 from cohort 3 and swap with spare rack-21 to avoid risk.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: id=mt-az9-20260514-01, window=2026-05-14T03:00:00Z..2026-05-14T07:00:00Z, cohorts=6. Notifying watchers: eng-infra, eng-oncall, cs, platform.

oncall: I'll be oncall for the window. escalation: pager for thermal alarms + 15m guard until cohort complete. If NVLink errors > 5% across a rack, abort and roll back to previous kernel image.

alex: cost question — any expected bump from spillover to eu-west? ballpark ops_estimate?

mike: short term burst to reserved capacity ~2-3% of monthly GPU hours for the region; estimated extra ~$7k for the window if we fully spill. We'll prefer spot backfill first and only bump reserved if latencies exceed SLOs.

sara: I'll send CS note with embedders mitigation and expected cost note. Will tag customers and post scheduled banner in console 24h and 1h before.

mike: timeline recap in runbook updated. Key runbook steps: 1) pre-flight health check + canary rack reboot, 2) cohort cordon & drain, 3) cache warmups (lia), 4) reboot + health probe, 5) uncordon + 30m observation, 6) proceed next cohort.

jordan: logs and dashboards to watch: pod_eviction_rate, prefix_cache_miss, nvlink_error_count, 99p_latency_per_region. I'll add a dashboard with cohort tagging.

mike: thanks — if no blockers I'll open the maintenance and ping CS. :thumbsup:
